findings.evidence: package.json devDependencies = { "typescript": "^5.9.3", "vitest": "^3.2.7" } (no @types/node); javaContract.ts:1 `import { existsSync, readdirSync, readFileSync } from "node:fs";` and :107 `return process.env[BACKEND_ROOT_ENV] ?? DEFAULT_BACKEND_ROOT;`. packages/api-client/node_modules holds only typescript and vitest (no @types), and there is no root node_modules/@types/node. pnpm-lock.yaml:156 resolves the api-client importer to `vitest@3.2.7(@types/node@20.19.43)(...)`: that peer variant exists only because apps/tenant-web (lock line 75) and apps/vendor-web (line 127) declare @types/node ^20 and pnpm merges the vitest peer variants.
findings.why_it_matters: OBS-P5-001 confirmed, and the mechanism is narrower than 'currently resolved transitively': the node types reach the api-client program only through vitest's d.ts reference, which pnpm resolves from a peer variant that is shared with the apps. Removing @types/node or vitest from tenant-web/vendor-web, a lockfile re-resolution, or a standalone install of the package would make `pnpm --filter @pte/api-client typecheck` (a Phase 5 success criterion) fail on javaContract.ts with TS2307/TS2580 while nothing in this package changed. Severity LOW (not MEDIUM): the lockfile pins the working resolution so today's behaviour is deterministic, it is test-support-only (no production source uses a Node API) and the fix is one line. Package source stays free of Node APIs, so the published/consumed surface is unaffected.
findings.required_action: Non-blocking, recommended with the next package.json touch: add "@types/node": "^20" to packages/api-client devDependencies (same range as both apps; lock currently resolves 20.19.43), run `pnpm install` so the lockfile importer entry gains it (the vitest key stays the same variant), then re-run `pnpm --filter @pte/api-client typecheck`. No tsconfig change needed (no `types` array is set, so @types/node is picked up automatically once declared). Do not add a `types` restriction that would hide it from the test helpers.

findings.evidence: Phase Preflight: 'types folders hold type-only barrels (no runtime constants ...)'. The same folder now holds runtime test support: fixtures/common.ts:19 `export const DASHBOARD_META_FIXTURE: DashboardMeta = {`, javaContract.ts:19 `export const BACKEND_ROOT_ENV = "PTE_API_JAVA_DIR";`, and a 190-line Java parser (javaRecords.ts). Leak check: package.json is `private: true`, `"main": "./src/index.ts"`, `"exports": { ".": "./src/index.ts", "./types": "./src/types/index.ts" }`, no `files` field and no build step (config tsconfig has `noEmit: true`); types/dashboard/index.ts exports only ./common ./host ./admin; no non-test file imports javaContract/javaWalker/javaRecords/fixtures (grep of imports: only *.test.ts files and fixtures themselves).
findings.why_it_matters: Answer to the leak question: NO leak into any published/built output or bundle today. There is no published output or build (source-consumed workspace package), the exports map blocks deep imports such as @pte/api-client/src/types/dashboard/javaContract, the barrels do not reference the helpers, and the bundlers only follow imports (the apps never import them). Residual risk is organisational, not mechanical: ~700 lines of test infrastructure (parser, walker, fixtures) sit in the production type folder, contradict the 'type-only barrel' convention recorded in the Preflight, and are protected only by a doc comment ('never exported from the package barrels'). Because tsconfig include is `src`, they are also part of every typecheck program of the package. Phases 6-8 will likely want the typed fixtures for component tests, and the exports map gives them no sanctioned path to import them.
findings.required_action: Non-blocking. Preferred: move the helpers and fixtures out of the types tree into a dedicated test-support folder under src (for example src/testing/dashboard/ for fixtures and src/testing/java/ for the parser/walker), keep it out of every barrel, and, only when Phases 6-8 need the fixtures, add an explicit "./testing" export instead of deep imports. If left where they are, add one sentence to the Phase 5 notes that these files are test-only so reviewers do not mistake them for contract code.

findings.evidence: const MAPPINGS = [ { file: "tenancy/RecentTenantView.java", source: "RecentTenantView", target: "AdminSectionData.RecentTenant", renames: { publicId: "tenantId", studentLimit: "seatLimit" } }, { file: "billing/BillingOverviewService.java", source: "LicenseCounts", ... }, ... 19 entries across tenancy, billing, support, identity, itembank, scoring, enrollment ];  plus the guard 'lists every record of the facade files it maps from (a new facade record needs a mapping decision)'. javaContract.ts:23 `const DEFAULT_BACKEND_ROOT = fileURLToPath(new URL("../../../../../../pte-api/app/src/main/java/com/pte", import.meta.url));` and `loadBackend()` runs at module import (contract.test.ts:48, contractFacade.test.ts:12).
findings.why_it_matters: Runtime coupling assessment. The core idea (read the Java overview records and compare with typed fixtures, both directions) is sound, deterministic (static files, no clock, no network), fast (~30 small files parsed twice at collection), skip-safe (visible it.skip entry, exit 0) and hard-fail-able with PTE_API_REQUIRED=1; the default sibling path is correct (6 levels up from types/dashboard reaches Capstore/pte-api) and PTE_API_JAVA_DIR overrides it. The mutation run in the test report proves the walker is not vacuous. The weak part is contractFacade.test.ts: it pins the internal file layout and nested-record names of eight backend modules (for example a record moved out of BillingOverviewService.java breaks it) although none of that is on the wire. Facade-to-response mapping is already the backend's own test responsibility (Phases 1-4), and the response-level walk in contract.test.ts already catches every wire-visible drift. The cost is a false red on developer machines that have the sibling checkout, fixed by editing a hand-maintained table. Also a malformed or newly annotated Java construct makes parseComponent throw during collection and fail the whole file instead of one test.
findings.required_action: Non-blocking. Either drop contractFacade.test.ts and keep the response-level conformance (the wire contract), or keep it but make it explicitly opt-in (for example only when PTE_API_REQUIRED=1) so routine runs on a dev machine do not depend on eight backend files' layout. Optionally move loadBackend() inside a beforeAll so a parser error fails one suite with a clear message rather than at import time.

findings.evidence: common.ts:52-55 `One calendar-month amount. amount is a JSON number (the backend BigDecimal): format it with Intl.NumberFormat for the series currency and never add amounts of different currencies.`; admin.ts:142-147 repeats it for current/previous. Phase 4 QUAL-001 required_action (1)-(3): record the VND-only / 2^53 assumption and make switching to string serialisation a hard precondition of enabling any non-VND currency.
findings.why_it_matters: Fidelity is correct: BigDecimal -> number, nullable Double -> number | null, Instant/UUID -> string. Items (2) of the Phase 4 recommendation (number type, Intl.NumberFormat per currency, never sum across currencies, never re-derive changePct: TrendValue docs say changePct is backend-computed) are carried into the types. The type documentation does not state the limit that makes `number` safe: exactness ends at the wire, safe up to 2^53 and only while currencies have no fractional digits (VND today, PlanRequest @Pattern VND). A future author enabling another currency, or a UI summing/rounding amounts, has no hint in the contract that this is a boundary. The fixtures also use fractional VND amounts (1500000.5) which contradicts the zero-decimal VND assumption the docs rely on.
findings.required_action: Non-blocking. Add one sentence to MonthlyAmount.amount / DashboardCurrencyRevenue.current-previous docs: 'Delivered as a JSON number; exact only up to 2^53 and for currencies the platform supports today (VND, zero decimals). Enabling a currency with fractional digits requires the backend to switch these fields to strings (or minor units) and this type to follow.' Keep the Intl.NumberFormat guidance. Optionally use an integer VND figure in the revenue fixtures and keep the fractional case only in a dedicated precision test.

findings.evidence: export type DashboardSectionStatus = "OK" | "ERROR" | "FORBIDDEN"; export interface DashboardSection<T> { status: DashboardSectionStatus; data: T | null; }  with the doc line 'data is non-null only when status is OK'. The test pins the loose shape: expectTypeOf<DashboardSection<number>>().toEqualTypeOf<{ status: DashboardSectionStatus; data: number | null }>().
findings.why_it_matters: Plan requirement met (status is an explicit union; no optional members anywhere, verified by the OptionalKeysOfUnion test; changePct is `number | null`). However the invariant that the Java Javadoc states (data null unless OK) is not expressible by consumers: `{ status: "OK", data: null }` and `{ status: "ERROR", data: {...} }` type-check, and `if (section.status === "OK")` does not narrow `data`, so every widget in Phases 6-8 must add a second `data !== null` check or a non-null assertion. Changing this now touches one type and its fixtures; after Phases 6-8 it touches every consumer.
findings.required_action: Non-blocking, cheap now. Consider `type DashboardSection<T> = { status: "OK"; data: T } | { status: "ERROR" | "FORBIDDEN"; data: null }` (keep DashboardSectionStatus as an alias of the three literals) and update the pinned type test and fixtures helpers (ok/forbidden/failed already map one-to-one). If the team prefers the flatter shape, record that decision in the phase notes so widgets standardise on one guard.

findings.evidence: next-env.d.ts:3 `import "./.next/dev/types/routes.d.ts";`; .gitignore ignores `.next/` and `next-env.d.ts`. apps/vendor-web/.next/dev/types/routes.d.ts: mtime 2026-10-10 08:16:05 (3 days before Phase 5 work), 3269 bytes; lines 55-61 show the route map cut off after the LayoutSlotMap block and a second fragment (`: {}`, `"/admin/licenses": {}`, ...) appended. tests/phase-05-baselines.md: with only the typecheck script added and no other change, vendor-web typecheck = 28 errors, all in that file; tenant-web = 0.
findings.why_it_matters: Baseline confirmed, not caused by this change: the corrupted generated file predates Phase 5 by three days, the 28 errors reproduce with the script as the only edit, they sit only in .next/dev/types/routes.d.ts, and the tester's throwaway tsconfig (same options, .next and next-env.d.ts excluded, 173 source files listed) is clean before and after Phase 5. The script itself is correct and minimal for this phase: additive, identical to the packages' `tsc --noEmit`, base config has noEmit/incremental so nothing is emitted (tsbuildinfo is gitignored). The design weakness: the result depends on mutable, gitignored generated state (a second concurrent `next dev` write corrupted it, and a fresh clone has neither next-env.d.ts nor .next/types), so the same command can be red for environmental reasons, or silently skip Next's global types, depending on the machine. A reviewer or CI cannot tell a real type error from a stale artifact without the baseline note.
findings.required_action: Non-blocking; acceptable for the phase as recorded. Hardening to schedule (not part of this gate): change both scripts to `next typegen && tsc --noEmit`, which the bundled Next 16 docs (docs/01-app/03-api-reference/06-cli/next.md, 'next typegen' section) describe exactly for CI type checking; it regenerates next-env.d.ts and the route types before tsc so the result no longer depends on whichever dev server last wrote them. Verify once on vendor-web that the regenerated next-env.d.ts no longer imports the corrupted dev routes file (otherwise delete apps/vendor-web/.next/dev/types/routes.d.ts once locally). Keep tenant-web symmetrical with vendor-web.

findings.location: pte-web/packages/api-client/package.json:11-14 ("test": "vitest run", no typecheck in test); pte-web/turbo.json:3-17 (tasks: build, dev, lint, test; no typecheck); pte-web/packages/api-client/src/types/dashboard/contract.test.ts:104-113
findings.evidence: contractTypes.test.ts:61-63 'The expectTypeOf assertions and the @ts-expect-error lines are enforced by the compiler (pnpm --filter @pte/api-client typecheck ...); at runtime they are no-ops.'  contract.test.ts:111 `it.skip(`SKIPPED dashboard contract conformance: ${message}`, () => undefined);`  No .github workflow exists in pte-web; turbo.json has no typecheck task and the root package.json has no typecheck script.
findings.why_it_matters: Two guards are weaker than the test report's wording suggests. (1) The type-level contract tests (no optional member, nullability, 6 @ts-expect-error cases) pass vacuously under `vitest run`; they are enforced only if someone runs `pnpm --filter @pte/api-client typecheck`, which neither `pnpm test` nor turbo does. A broken @ts-expect-error would not fail the test run. (2) The backend conformance is skipped (exit 0) wherever pte-api is not a sibling checkout, which is where a CI would run, so contract drift is detectable only locally until Phase 9's live check. Both match the plan constraint 'Tests do not require a running backend' and are a deliberate trade-off, but the gap should be visible to the next phases.
findings.required_action: None for this gate. Track: add a `typecheck` task to turbo.json (and a root `typecheck` script) so the type-level assertions are enforced by the same pipeline, or enable vitest `typecheck` for *.test.ts; set PTE_API_REQUIRED=1 in any pipeline that has both repos checked out; document PTE_API_JAVA_DIR / PTE_API_REQUIRED where developers will look (currently only in test comments and the phase file).

findings.evidence: Design Constraints: 'Sections not yet delivered by the backend are typed optional/nullable ... the map section is optional until Phase 10.' Step 3: '... and reuse existing audit-log and session-status types.' Implementation: no optional member anywhere (contractTypes.test.ts:106-108 `expectTypeOf<OptionalKeysOfUnion<AllContractObjects>>().toEqualTypeOf<never>()`), no map field in AdminDashboardResponse, and DashboardActivityItem (host.ts:117-123) is dedicated rather than AuditLogResponse.
findings.why_it_matters: Both deviations are correct and evidenced: every Java record component is always serialised (ApiResponse is @JsonInclude(ALWAYS), no NON_NULL config in the overview module), AuditLogResponse has publicId/aggregateType/aggregateId/summary/createdAt while ActivityItem has id/action/actorUserId/targetType/occurredAt, so reuse would be wrong; the Preflight records the audit-log non-reuse but not the 'no optional members' decision, so the Design Constraints text still tells the Phase 6-9 authors to expect optional sections. Reused shared unions: SessionStatus, PlanType, SubscriptionStatus, ActivationSource, QuestionStatus, QuestionPool, TicketCategory, TenantStatusResponse (all equal the Java enums per the conformance run); new types are justified only where no existing type fits.
findings.required_action: None blocking. Reword the Design Constraint to 'every backend component is always present; absence is expressed as section status plus null data; the map section is added additively in Phase 10'.

findings.location: pte-web/packages/api-client/src/requests/dashboard/index.test.ts:13,24-29 vs dashboardTestUtils.ts:6,8-13; index.edgeCases.test.ts:35-43 vs requests/endpoints.test.ts:20-28; index.test.ts:65-83 vs index.edgeCases.test.ts:82-90
findings.evidence: index.test.ts redefines `const BASE_URL = "https://api.example.test";` and `function jsonResponse(body: unknown, status = 200): Response {...}` which dashboardTestUtils.ts exports; index.edgeCases.test.ts copies RETIRED_SERVICE_SEGMENTS although endpoints.test.ts:80-103 already auto-discovers DASHBOARD_ENDPOINTS (plan step 5; baselines.md notes +4 discovered checks); windowDays=7/30/90 URL assertions appear in both files.
findings.why_it_matters: Tests are meaningful and non-vacuous (exact URL, plain GET without body, real-client envelope unwrap, error kinds, 401 refresh, mutated-fixture and mutated-Java checks), named by behaviour, well isolated (fetch mocked, no timers), all files <= 300 lines (largest 274: index.test.ts; others 237/254/239/216/149), and fast. The repetition is harmless duplication across a cook-written and a tester-written suite; the second copy of the retired-segment list can drift from the first. Hand-rolled Java parsing (~700 lines incl. tests/walker/tables) is a notable maintenance investment for a ~340-line contract; a generated OpenAPI snapshot from the backend would replace it long term.
findings.required_action: None required. Optional tidy: make index.test.ts import BASE_URL/jsonResponse from dashboardTestUtils and drop the duplicated RETIRED_SERVICE_SEGMENTS copy (endpoints.test.ts already covers the constant). Consider an OpenAPI-based contract check later instead of parsing Java.

findings.evidence: byStatus: Record<SessionStatus, number>; activatedBySource: Record<ActivationSource, number>; byType: Record<PlanType, number>; export const DASHBOARD_WINDOW_OPTIONS = [7, 30, 90] as const satisfies readonly DashboardWindowDays[];  getHostDashboard(client, windowDays?) takes no RequestOptions although ApiClient.request accepts RequestInit (client.ts:42,85) and siblings (scheduling/sessions.ts, admin/examStaffWorkspace.ts) pass a signal.
findings.why_it_matters: Forward-compat notes, not defects. (1) Record<Enum, number> says every key is present; true today (backend zero-fills from the enum) but an enum constant added to the backend before the web union would give a runtime-missing key typed as number. The conformance suite catches it only where the sibling checkout exists. (2) `satisfies readonly DashboardWindowDays[]` only checks that offered windows are valid, not that every union member is offered; adding 180 to the union would not force the options array. (3) Window changes in the dashboard UI will trigger refetches; TanStack Query supplies an AbortSignal that these functions cannot forward. All are additive to fix later.
findings.required_action: None. Re-check when the first new enum constant or window is introduced; when Phase 6 wires TanStack Query, add an optional trailing `options?: RequestOptions` (signal) to both functions, which is backward compatible.

verification_notes.contract_fidelity: Compared every Java record in overview/internal/dto/response (HostSectionData 11 nested records, AdminSectionData 14 nested records, DashboardMeta, DashboardSection, SectionStatus, TrendValue, MonthlyPoint, MonthlyAmount, both roots) and the two serialised facade records (UpcomingSessionView, CurrentSubscriptionView) with host.ts/admin.ts/common.ts. Names, component order and sets match 1:1 (MonthlySeries is cache-only and correctly absent). Nullability: exactly the 10 documented nullable components are `| null` (TrendValue.changePct, CurrencyRevenue.changePct, UpcomingSession.capacity, Subscription.planName/planType, HostSubscription.nearestExpiryAt/daysToExpiry, RecentTenant.planName/subscriptionExpiresAt, OldestTicket.tenantName); all other primitives/UUID/String are non-null and non-optional. Kinds: long/int/double/BigDecimal -> number, Instant/UUID -> string (ISO-8601), boolean -> boolean. Enum strings narrowed by reuse of existing unions: SessionStatus, PlanType, SubscriptionStatus, ActivationSource, QuestionStatus, QuestionPool, TicketCategory, TenantStatusResponse (ACTIVE|SUSPENDED equals TenantStatus). Maps: enum-keyed ones are Record<Union, number>; bySection and byOrganizationType are Record<string, number> (documented: stored/unknown section names). windowDays 7|30|90 and the SectionStatus union equal the backend constants. No templates, platform-health, payment-link, system-notice or map field exists in any type (HostBillingData is a count only; AdminSupportData omits resolvedAwaitingClose like the Java record). No fidelity defect found.
verification_notes.conventions: Matches siblings: `*_ENDPOINTS` const object with full /api/v1 path (quota/index.ts, platformCommercial.ts), client-first functions returning client.request<T>(...) (already unwrapped; errors propagate as ApiError untouched, pinned by tests), URLSearchParams query like pageQuery in platformCommercial.ts, barrel `export * from "./dashboard"` in both requests/index.ts:45 and types/index.ts:23. Constants (DASHBOARD_WINDOW_OPTIONS, DEFAULT_DASHBOARD_WINDOW_DAYS) live in requests, consistent with the rule that types folders hold no runtime values and with DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE living in client/client.ts. UPPER_SNAKE constants, PascalCase types, explicit return types on both exported functions, no `any`, no @ts-ignore (every @ts-expect-error carries a reason), no TanStack code, no user-facing strings. Production files 60/138/196/3/39 lines; all test and support files <= 274 lines.
verification_notes.public_api_surface: No name collision: TrendValue, MonthlyPoint, MonthlyAmount, DashboardSection*, Dashboard*, Host*Data, Admin*Data, DASHBOARD_* and getHostDashboard/getAdminDashboard are defined nowhere else in pte-web (repo-wide grep; only the dashboard files and their tests match). Naming is consistent: section payloads are Host<Section>Data / Admin<Section>Data, nested rows and shared pieces are Dashboard<Row> (the prefix avoids clashing with existing Subscription/Tenant/Ticket types). Export count (about 34 types, 5 values) is what the UI needs; nothing test-related is exported. Non-reuse of AuditLogResponse is justified (field set differs, see QUAL-008).
verification_notes.published_output_and_bundler: api-client is private, source-consumed (`main`/`types` -> src/index.ts), has no build script, no `files` field, and the config base tsconfig has noEmit; there is therefore no published or built artifact that could include test helpers. The exports map exposes only `.` and `./types`, so bundlers/TS (moduleResolution: bundler) cannot deep-import javaContract/javaWalker/fixtures. Apps pull the package through the barrels only, and no barrel imports the helpers. App tsc programs follow imports, not the package's include glob, so *.test.ts files are not type-checked by the apps. Node APIs appear only in javaContract.ts (node:fs, node:path, node:url, process); the package source has none.
verification_notes.baseline_confirmation: vendor-web typecheck red is a baseline environment issue, not caused by Phase 5: corrupted generated apps/vendor-web/.next/dev/types/routes.d.ts (mtime 2026-10-10 08:16, truncated map plus appended fragment), pulled in through next-env.d.ts:3, reproduced by baselines.md with the script as the only change (28 errors, all in that file), 0 errors elsewhere and 0 with the file excluded, before and after the api-client changes; tenant-web typecheck 0 errors.
verification_notes.tests_not_rerun: This review was read-only. I did not execute tests, typecheck or lint (running them writes tsbuildinfo/.vite caches); results are taken from tests/phase-05-test-report.json and tests/phase-05-baselines.md (api-client 28 files / 570 tests, 0 failed, 0 skipped when the sibling backend is present; typecheck clean; tenant-web typecheck/test/lint and vendor-web lint at baseline).
verification_notes.test_quality: Not vacuous: request tests assert exact URLs, absence of body, falsy-value passthrough (0, NaN, null forwarded verbatim), real-client envelope unwrap and ApiError kinds; contract tests walk 11 typed fixtures against the Java records in both directions at every depth, require every record of the DTO package to be reached and every nullable to be seen as null, and include a self-test with mutated fixtures; the tester also ran a mutated copy of the Java sources (9 expected failures). Deterministic and fast (no time, network, randomness). Skip-when-absent: visible it.skip and PTE_API_REQUIRED=1 turns absence into a failure. Weak spots are in QUAL-003 and QUAL-007.
verification_notes.receipt_note: Verdict is APPROVED, but this review was run read-only with the report as the only permitted write, so scripts/receipt.py was NOT invoked; the caller (ck:cook) must issue the receipt from this report if it wants one.
